dependency_notes: Ordering follows the lead's explicit staging: pure core (S1-S3) -> raw-event-log persistence (S4) -> engine FSM (S5-S6) -> adapter (S7) -> React integration (S8) -> UI read-path cutover (S9) -> publish/outbox (S10, Phase 6) -> recovery persistence (S11, Phase 7) -> legacy removal (S12, Phase 8) -> hardening (S13, Phase 9). This mirrors spec.md's Phase 1-9 migration but reorders Phase-3/4 UI cutover ahead of Phase-6 outbox and Phase-7 recovery, per the lead's instruction to sequence by module dependency rather than raw phase number; Phase 3's shadow/parallel-run mechanism was rejected by ADR-002 and downgraded to listener-observation-only, so it produces no dedicated story or AC of its own -- it is satisfied as a side effect of S3 (task-projector) + S4 (raw-event-log-store) landing before S9's feature-flagged cutover, which is the observation/comparison point. EXPLICIT SHARED MODULE OWNERSHIP (Validation Checks exception): receive-engine is owned by S5 (core FSM, Phase 5), S6 (ingest hardening, Phase 5 continuation), and S11 (recovery sequencing, Phase 7) -- the epic's own phase structure separates these concerns onto the same file at different times, each independently testable via its own AC subset and its own mock boundary. marmot-adapter is owned by S7 (Phase 5, IngestSource/IngestSignal) and S10 (Phase 6, outbox bridge) for the same reason. task-store is owned by S9 (Phase 4 cutover, delegation-only) and S12 (Phase 8 removal, deletion-only) -- both are Boundary-Rule-5-compliant (no new decision logic). ingest-policy.ts (S5), checkpoint-store.ts and deferred-store.ts (S11) are folded into their sole consumer's story rather than given standalone stories: none of the 35 ACs tests them in isolation (they are thin CRUD/wrapper modules with no independent behavioral contract), and Story Design Principle 3 (vertical slices) disfavors a horizontal story with no observable result. `specs/epic-event-sourced-receive-engine/**` is implicitly in scope for every story (state bookkeeping) and is not repeated in each story's scope.includes.
mock_resolution_plan: MOCK-05-001 (mock IngestSource/IngestSignal producer) is introduced in S5 to unit-test the FSM without live marmot-ts wiring; resolved when S7 lands the real marmot-adapter.ts implementation of the same IngestSource contract. MOCK-05-002 (mock checkpoint/deferred persistence methods) is introduced in S5, also consumed by S6; resolved when S11 lands real checkpoint-store.ts/deferred-store.ts and wires R1-R4 recovery. Both mocks are internal to receive-engine's unit-test suite only -- no production code path depends on them, and neither blocks any story's independent verifiability since each mocked contract is frozen in S1 (engine-types.ts) before any consumer is planned.

invariants: id is the primary dedupe key; appendAcceptedEvent is idempotent on id
MLS path: id = rumor.id from the applicationMessage callback
bootstrap path: id = `bootstrap:${groupId}:${task.id}`, deterministic across re-runs
replay sort order over a mixed-sourceKind log is phase order (bootstrap before MLS), never acceptedAt clock order
carries no marmot-ts types; payload is the app's own TaskEvent wire type
catchUp() must be drained to completion before openLive() is invoked for the same group
epoch_advanced maps to group_epoch_advanced + deferred-retry flush; a bare ratchet advance produces no signal
malformed is terminal: engine emits domain_event_rejected{reason:parse_error}, never parked, never retried

intermediaries.artifact: src/engine/receive-engine.ts (consumes via MOCK-05-001 during FSM development)

invariants: all IDB keys used by implementations are defined in src/engine/engine-types.ts (Boundary Rule 8)

intermediaries.artifact: src/engine/receive-engine.ts (checkpoint/deferred methods mocked via MOCK-05-002 pending S11)

fields.name: type
fields.type: discriminated union: envelope_received | envelope_deferred | domain_event_accepted | domain_event_rejected | projection_invalidated | group_epoch_advanced | group_ratchet_advanced | engine_state_changed | deferred_retry_started | recovered

invariants: projection_invalidated MUST NOT be emitted on ratchet-advance stateChanged
on domain_event_accepted the integration layer MUST call applyEvent incrementally, never buildProjection

stories.name: raw-event-log-store
stories.title: Idempotent Raw-Fact and Accepted-Event Log Store
stories.description: Author src/persistence/raw-event-log-store.ts implementing the fact/accepted-event half of PersistenceAdapter (appendFact, loadFacts, appendAcceptedEvent, loadAcceptedEvents) as idempotent, lookup-before-insert IDB stores using createKVStore, replacing persistence.ts:appendEvent's read-modify-write with no idempotency key. From this point on, no file other than src/store/persistence.ts's pre-existing implementation may write to the legacy notestr:events:${groupId} key.

excludes: no writes to notestr:events:${groupId} outside src/store/persistence.ts's pre-existing implementation

stories.notes: AC-MIG-1's grep test is written here (the trigger point per its own text: 'from Phase 2, once raw-event-log-store.ts exists, onward') and re-runs as a CI gate at every later phase-boundary commit as a regression net; ownership stays with S4. CONTRACT AMENDED 2026-07-12: appendFact(RawProtocolFactInput) -> AppendFactResult — the store is the sole seq authority; duplicates return the existing fact/seq with duplicate:true. acceptDeferredFact is NOT this story (S11 owns it); no cross-store co-location required (revised R-INV-3 uses accepted-first ordering, not a transaction). ORDERING CONTRACT (S3 review sev-5, 2026-07-12): loadFacts returns seq-ascending (= append) order; loadAcceptedEvents returns APPEND order (assign a monotonic position on append; never content-hash-id order — idb-keyval keys() sorts by key and would silently break projection determinism). S4 tests MUST assert order preservation across a real store->load round-trip incl. a delete-before-update interleaving. AC-INV-2 SPLIT GATE (S3 closure): this story MUST prove appendAcceptedEvent idempotency on event.id (lookup-before-insert) — the projector formally depends on it (unique-id-log precondition); S4 cannot close without that proof.

stories.name: receive-engine-core-fsm

stories.name: receive-engine-ingest-hardening

stories.description: Extend receive-engine.ts (built in S5) with the two failure-mode defaults added by the 2026-07-12 spec validation: a failing appendFact/appendAcceptedEvent/saveCheckpoint call sets health degraded, retains the fact in memory, and retries with bounded backoff without silent discard (Implementation Constraint 11); a malformed IngestSignal produces a terminal domain_event_rejected{reason:parse_error}, never enqueued to the deferred queue, never retried on a later epoch_advanced (Implementation Constraint 13).

CONTRACT AMENDED 2026-07-12: adapter produces RawProtocolFactInput (seq-less) facts in ALL IngestSignal variants incl. skipped; must implement ingestPersisted(facts) as 4th IngestSource method — include it in the AC-ADPT-1 fidelity matrix. S7 IMPLEMENTS fetchBootstrap() (5th IngestSource method, amended 2026-07-12): NIP-44 kind-30078 fetch+decode yielding bootstrap-kind-30078 message signals sharing the snapshot fact; MUST be safe to overlap catchUp/openLive (never touches the ratchet); MUST tolerate continuing past T_join (no abandonment). catchUp() contract: exactly once per engine start, never concurrent with itself.

stories.name: recovery-sequencing
stories.title: Recovery Persistence: Checkpoint/Deferred Stores and R1-R4 Sequencing
stories.description: Author src/persistence/checkpoint-store.ts and src/persistence/deferred-store.ts (real IDB implementations, resolving MOCK-05-002), and wire the Recovery Sequencing R1-R4 steps into receive-engine.ts: R1 rebuild projection via buildProjection(replayOrder(acceptedLog)); R2 repopulate PendingRetryQueue from deferredIds without resubmitting to ingest; R3 resubmit only rawLog facts with seq > checkpoint.lastIngestedSeq; R4 transition recovering->catching_up and resume live drain. Also handles the malformed/unreadable-checkpoint-at-restart failure mode (treat as absent, never escalate to reset()).
stories.notes: checkpoint-store.ts and deferred-store.ts are folded into this story rather than given their own earlier stories because none of the 35 ACs tests their round-trip persistence in isolation -- their entire behavioral contract is the R1-R4 recovery sequencing proven here (Phase 7, 'Persist recovery metadata explicitly'). Resolves MOCK-05-002 introduced in S5. Shares owning_module with S5/S6; justified in top-level dependency_notes. CONTRACT AMENDED 2026-07-12: S11 owns PersistenceAdapter.acceptDeferredFact (accepted-first crash-safe ordering per revised R-INV-3 — append accepted, then remove deferred) AND the new R2a prune step (deferred ∩ accepted -> prune, accepted wins) which runs before R2. Also wires IngestSource.ingestPersisted for R3 crash-gap replay and L8 deferred retry. CLEAR-ORDERING INVARIANT (S4 review, 2026-07-12): full clearGroupState spans >=2 IDB databases (non-atomic). Clear the CHECKPOINT FIRST: a crash mid-reset must degrade toward L2-joining / L1-second-arm, never leave a usable bootstrapCompleted checkpoint over already-emptied logs (stranded empty recovery). Compose S4 exported clearGroupState partial for raw/accepted stores; reuse S4 appendAcceptedEvent inside acceptDeferredFact.
